title: Weak finite-order Gårding estimate on a compact bundle
statement: All vector spaces are over $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field]. Let $N$ be a compact oriented smooth manifold without boundary of dimension $m\geq1$, with a smooth Riemannian metric and its positive volume form. For a smooth finite-rank real metric bundle $B$, let $L^2(B)$ be measurable square-integrable sections modulo almost-everywhere equality. For an integer $j\geq0$, let $H^j(B)$ be the subspace of $L^2(B)$ whose local coefficients in smooth coordinate charts and bundle frames have distributional derivatives through order $j$ locally in $L^2$. Fix Sobolev norms $\|\cdot\|_{H^j}$ obtained by a finite smooth coordinate trivializing cover and a subordinate smooth partition of unity, taking the square root of the sum of squared Euclidean $L^2$ norms of all derivatives through order $j$ of the localized sections. Here $H^0(B)=L^2(B)$, with its usual integrated norm $\|\cdot\|_{L^2}$. Distributional derivatives are taken by duality against compactly supported smooth test functions in each chart. Let $B$ be such a bundle and let $P:\Gamma^\infty(B)\to\Gamma^\infty(B)$ be a real-linear differential operator with smooth coefficients of order at most an integer $d\geq1$. Write it locally as $P=\sum_{|\alpha|\leq d}a_\alpha(x)\partial^\alpha$, and assume the degree-$d$ symbol $\sum_{|\alpha|=d}a_\alpha(x)\xi^\alpha:B_x\to B_x$ is invertible for every $\xi\neq0$. For each integer $s\geq0$ there is a constant $C_s>0$, depending on $P$, the fixed geometry, the chosen norms and $s$, such that for every $v\in L^2(B)$ for which the distribution $Pv$ belongs to $H^s(B)$, one has $$v\in H^{s+d}(B),\qquad \|v\|_{H^{s+d}}\leq C_s\bigl(\|Pv\|_{H^s}+\|v\|_{L^2}\bigr).$$ The distribution $Pv$ means applying the local differential expression to the coefficients of $v$ using distributional derivatives; its membership in $H^s(B)$ means equality with the distribution induced by an element of that space. No a priori $H^{s+d}$ regularity of $v$ is required.

source.place: WANTED locally; Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, June 21, 2012, VI §2, weak Gårding inequality (2.3), printed p.289 (PDF page 289), finite-order regularity and norm estimate for an operator on one bundle; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-elliptic-distribution-parametrix] with $C=B$ to obtain $A\in\Psi^{-d}(B,B)$ and a smooth-kernel operator $R_K$ satisfying $AP=\mathrm{id}+R_K$ on all distributions. Its hypotheses are exactly compactness, absence of boundary, smooth real coefficients and invertibility of the degree-$d$ symbol assumed here. Fix $s\geq0$ and write $f\in H^s(B)$ for the section inducing $Pv$; the identity therefore gives $v=Af-R_Kv$ in $\mathcal D'(B)$, even though $v$ was assumed only in $L^2$.

source.place: Part I 3.B, construction after 3.8 and proof of 3.9, printed pp.13–14; WANTED locally; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/hodge-ams.pdf

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-symbol-operator-sobolev-boundedness] for $A$, with order $r=-d$ and input index $t=s$. Both $t$ and $t-r=s+d$ are nonnegative. It follows that $Af\in H^{s+d}(B)$ and $\|Af\|_{H^{s+d}}\leq a_s\|f\|_{H^s}$ for a positive constant $a_s$ fixed by $A$ and the chosen data. This is the action on the distribution $f=Pv$, as required in the identity from step 1.

source.place: Part I Theorem 3.6, used in the proof of 3.9, printed pp.13–14; WANTED locally; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/hodge-ams.pdf

proof.text: In [def-sfb-symbol-pseudodifferential-operators], take the empty local-symbol sum and kernel $K$. Thus the same $R_K$ belongs to $\Psi^{-(s+d)}(B,B)$; the definition imposes no restriction on the integer order for the smooth-kernel term. Apply [lem-sfb-symbol-operator-sobolev-boundedness] with $t=0$ and $r=-(s+d)$. Since $H^0=L^2$, this gives $R_Kv\in H^{s+d}(B)$ and $\|R_Kv\|_{H^{s+d}}\leq b_s\|v\|_{L^2}$, with $b_s>0$.

source.place: Part I 3.B, Theorem 3.6 and following smooth-kernel paragraph, printed p.13; WANTED locally; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/hodge-ams.pdf

proof.text: The difference $w=Af-R_Kv$ belongs to $H^{s+d}(B)$: its local weak derivatives are the differences of the corresponding $L^2$ derivatives. The distribution identity gives $v=w$. The injectivity of $L^2(B)\to\mathcal D'(B)$ in [lem-sfb-bundle-sobolev-rellich] identifies their $L^2$ classes, so $v\in H^{s+d}(B)$. The triangle inequality and the preceding two bounds yield $\|v\|_{H^{s+d}}\leq a_s\|Pv\|_{H^s}+b_s\|v\|_{L^2}\leq C_s(\|Pv\|_{H^s}+\|v\|_{L^2})$, where $C_s=\max(1,a_s,b_s)>0$. None of these constants depends on $v$.
